content:
maya: heads up — saw a weird spike in JSON parse failures from the tool-calling eval harness after we landed the batching KV-cache optimizer yesterday

alex: saw that too. failures are ~0.6% on canary, mostly `parse error: unexpected token` when expecting function call objects

jun: uploading short example that reproduces locally with 4 concurrent requests + continuous batching enabled. seems non-deterministic but much higher when batch size >1

maya: repro snippet: ```bash
# run 4 parallel requests against local runtime
ab --concurrency 4 -n 200 http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -p payload.json
```

maya: sample failing output (trimmed): ```json
{"id":"req-123","choices":[{"message":{"role":"tool","name":"search","content":"{\"query\":\"s3 buckets\"}"}}]}
{"id":"req-124","choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Use this tool:\n\n{\"name\":\"search\", \"arguments\": {\"query\": \"s3 buckets\"}}"}}]}
```

jun: notice the second response interleaves a plain assistant message that contains the previous request's tool JSON as inline text. parser sees the plain text chunk and chokes when trying to extract func call JSON

alex: hypothesis: KV cache reuse for prefixes + batching is causing token stream to include cached tokens from prior request in the same batch window. for toolcall routes we expect strict prefix isolation

tara: ops-bot reported a deploy at 1821999000 that toggled "aggressive-kv-merge" on for perf tests 

ops-bot: deploy maya/kv-merge toggled to ON in staging at 1821999000. Canary rollout to 10% at 1821999400.

maya: ok that matches timing. when batch combines requests, the runtime concatenates cached prefix chunks and then slices per-request, but the slice boundaries for streamed toolcall JSON can fall inside a previously cached assistant message — yields garbled output

jun: quick mitigation: disable cross-request KV reuse for any route with `tool_calling: strict` in the model profile. cheap toggle and low perf impact since toolcall routes are smaller traffic fraction

alex: agree. longer term we should make KV cache boundary-aware of structured output tokens, or treat function-call markers as atomic when caching.

maya: also saw a small correlation with int8 quantized model builds — tokenization/decoding timing changes made batching windows align differently, increasing odds of mis-slice. but primary root is KV merging logic

jun: proposed patch: 
1) add per-request KV epoch id so cached chunks are only reused if epoch matches
2) add config `disable_kv_merge_for_toolcalls` default true for now
3) add unit test that simulates concurrent batches and asserts no interleaved JSON in function call output

alex: will open infra PR to gate this toggle per-route. canary patch to 1% immediately.

maya: test harness update notes: add randomized interleaving in the eval runner (spawn N virtual users with variable token emission rates) — caught things that deterministic single-run tests missed

tara: ops: before rolling to prod, can we instrument a fast metric: `toolcall_structured_parse_errors_per_1k` and alert at 1? we shouldn't roll forward with regressions

ops-bot: metric `toolcall_structured_parse_errors_per_1k` created on staging. alert threshold 1.00.

jun: timeline: I'll push the patch to branch `kv-toolcall-safety` today, alex will canary and we monitor metric for 2 hours, then widen if green

maya: adding note for release: this is likely to reduce a small perf win from KV merge but keeps structured-output correctness. add to changelog: "Disable KV merging on strict tool-call routes; add safety tests for batch interleaving"

alex: sounds good. tagging @eng-oncall for awareness.

maya: thanks everyone. follow-up: we'll evaluate if quantized decoding differences need an extra guard next week when we run the int8 bring-up bench

jun: ack. I'll paste the PR link when up.
